messages.content: Alonsa wakes up in her room in the Narita Inn. The second bed in the room is currently not in use.
What?
Wait, no, wait… what just happened?
Alonsa grips her head. It aches like it hasn’t before.
She stands up to get her bearings, and uses a nearby pitcher to wash her face. It doesn’t help.
Nightmares about her life were one thing. Even if the last one was especially vivid, it’s not something she hadn’t gotten used to by now.
But this was odd. She was in someone else’s body, she could feel what she felt, every minor sensation
Someone from centuries ago…
The last image of the dream lingered in her mind. She dresses herself and heads downstairs
The old man sits behind the desk as usual. To the side of the lobby are Briar and Cory, who seem to be in the midst of a conversation.
Briar wakes up in her room in the Narita Inn.
She exits her room and walks towards the lobby.
The old man is behind the desk as usual, but there's an additional presence. Cory sits in a chair, waiting for something. He spots her descending to the lobby, and gives a wave.
She walks towards him with a weak smile "Good morning"

He hesitates for a few seconds on what to say, before returning her smile. "Yes. We should talk."

Alonsa descends the stairs.
Alonsa descends into the lobby where Briar, Cory, and the old man are already present.
Briar turns her head to look at Alonsa and waves
“…Heya. Morning.”
The old man makes a vague gesture towards Alonsa. "Hey. Had someone in here earlier askin' 'bout you. Said to tell you her name was... Chef, the Chef. Friend o' yours?"
“Ohhhh… her!”
“Kind of a friend. What was she asking about?”
"Just said she needed to talk to you 'bout somethin'. Said she'd be waitin' at the town square."
“I’ll head there in a bit.”
“Hey, uhhh… how old is this desk?”
She indicates towards the desk that the old man sits

Cory stands up, and takes Briar's hand. "...Why don't we take a walk? I could use some fresh air."

The old man looks down at the desk, and runs his hand across it. "It was here when I got the inn from my old man... Had to be about... Hm..."
“How long has it been in the family?”
Briar gets startled and looks at his hand "Sure...", she looks at Alonsa and the old man
Cory leads Briar out of the inn.
The old man gives Alonsa a confused look. "Well, it's a desk. They're not exactly... family heirlooms. The inn's been around more than a few generations, back as far as the family records..."
Alonsa sighs
“This is going to sound insane.”
“I had a dream with this desk in it.”
“Specifically… that there was something in that drawer. Someone put it there… a long time ago.”

"Fairly regular to dream of where you sleep, I reckon. If you're curious, I can show you the drawer's contents, but it ain't nothin' special." He opens the drawer as he speaks, and slides his chair back to make room for Alonsa.
Alonsa looks inside.
There's plenty of odds and ends in the desk. A ledger, some trinkets, and some loose change. There is also, of course, a key. The very same.
Alonsa grabs the key.
“How long has this been here?”

He reaches to stop her, but pulls his hand back. "...That's... Well... That's funny. Feelin' a bit of déjà vu here... Like I've done this before, y'know?" He scratches his head. " ...Uh, right, well, key's been there since... the door to the church... well, it's gone now, so... I 'spose they must've removed it?"
“There’s something… something incredibly strange going on in that church.”
“You don’t mind if I hold onto this?” She asks, politely but firmly
"...I don't got any use for it. 'Cept as a paperweight, maybe." He waves his hand dismissively. "Go ahead, it's got a bad mood 'round it."
No kidding.
Alonsa stares at it. All the magic she has ever seen in her life has been simple tricks. Small fires or dancing lights…
What was happening here? Was she experiencing visions of the past? True and accurate ones?
Or was it something else…
The church changes itself each day. The runes on the walls exist one day and don’t exist the next. Alonsa seems to be the only one noticing. Could this be related?
She stuffs the key in her bag.
“Thank you. I appreciate it a lot.”
She heads out of the inn.
Briar and Cory have already wandered off, but there's a handful of other townsfolk going about their day. Normal life seems to have returned to the town, despite the previous day's events.
Alonsa looks at the church
It's grown. Again. It's nearly twice as tall today.
She stares at it, in silent awe
Maybe the church isn’t what’s changing. Maybe it’s history itself that changes every night.
If that’s true…. It means that she has a lot more work ahead of her.
She walks to wherever Chef is

Alonsa arrives at the town square. 'Chef' is staring at the golden statue. It's been sectioned off, and Yondovan royal guards stand at attention around it. The body's been removed, with only an outline remaining on the ground.
“Hey!”
“You wanted to see me?”
She's startled by the loud greeting, and shrinks back. After a moment, she straightens herself, and squeaks out a response. "Y-yes... Yes! I, um, that's true..."
“How’s it hanging?”
“Or…”
She looks at the site where the body was.
“Where’d he go?”
"An, uh, a-an, well... it'd be, like, an autopsy, probably... on th-the, uh, body..." Her hands start to shake, before she quickly clasps them together.
“Probably makes sense.”
“Is it a bad idea to go visit the prison? I wanna make sure Thromb is okay.”
"How, w-would I... know??" She squeezes her hands. "B-but, um, I wanted to talk, a-about... the..."
“The what?”

Chef shifts her position, placing her hand on her chest. With this action, something about her becomes clear to Alonsa. The Emperor's outline isn't the only recognizable one present at the town square. Chef's body is an exact match for the third hole near the locked door.

"I see it. Th-the church. It's... bigger."
“Oh.”
“Oh!”
“Well that’s good. That’s good!”
“Means I’m not going crazy.”
“…and Briar also said she could see it.”
“Ugh.”
“There’s something wrong here. This can’t be… it can’t be…”

"...Y-yeah. Um. Definitely, a... bad omen. I've never, been, uh, religious, but... it's like I've been cursed to s-see the... the monument to my sins... o-or maybe, I... cursed myself?" She prattles on about something or other.
((End session))
“No such thing as bad omens.”
“Which means… that this is something deliberate..”
"Y-you mean... s-someone's, uh, making it... bigger? On p-purpose?" She tries to follow Alonsa's reasoning.
“I don’t know.”

“But here’s what I know. The church is changing. And it’s not just the church itself, but the inside, maybe even the catacombs underneath. The languages on the walls are something I’ve never seen before, and they shift every day.”
“I can see that the church is changing. You can too. And we’re both here now.”

"...M-my brother... U-um, have you, t-talked to Tanner, about... it? H-he thinks that church, um... i-it's like... the womb, for humanity...? M-maybe it's alive, a-and it's... it's angry... b-because..." She starts biting her nails, and her whole body begins to shake.
“Tanner’s your brother?!?”

"Yeah..." She kind of looks like she's going to throw up. "Y-you're Alonsa, right...? H-he's always... spoken really highly, uh, of your, um, work... Th-thank you for, h-helping him... being th-there. I think he, uh, can kind of... neglect, s-some things..."
“Hmph…”
“Well, I’m glad he speaks so highly of me.”
“I owe him a lot.”
“We have a few big disagreements in… let’s say priorities of research. But he’s got a passion for it that rivals my own, and he’s always good at keeping an open mind.“
“He was always a lot more fixated on the mystical and magical elements of history. I like to focus on the smaller stuff.”

“That being said, I think your brother might be right. Not about the details, that’s probably a little too out there, yknow, but just… that something strange is happening. There’s some kind of force at work that’s altering that church and it’s got something to do with you and me.”
“Let me ask you, why did you come to this town? Or, more importantly, did you come here of your own free will?”

"...Why did I..." She stares at the golden statue, at a loss for words for a moment. "...I-I guess I wanted to... t-to make m-myself... I had such an easy life... I j-just wanted to be f-f-filthy, b-because... he was always... s-so! So!!!" She starts scratching at her arms, almost tearing into them with her nails, as her voice sounds as if it's tearing against her throat. "I'll do it! B-because... it was always h-him! I'll m-make myself filthy so no one else has to!"
Alonsa pauses for a second
“Going to be real with you I have no idea what that means.”

"I d-didn't want to... b-but if I didn't... someone else would! H-he'd just... th-that hand, he reached o-out and... I n-needed to, b-because someone else... th-they... I couldn't st-stop the filth... I j-just needed... all on me... I-I'll be the only filthy one! S-so why..." She falls to her knees. "W-why is this town... still so filthy..." Her eyes roll back as she spits these words out, and her head limply falls to the sand-coated ground.
“Hey… hey! Are you okay?”
Alonsa rushes over to her
She checks her pulse
She's alive, just passed out.
“Jeez Louise…”

She doesn’t realize it. Alonsa thought that she made a choice to come here, but she realized now that, through the machinations of others or perhaps fate itself, she was always going to come here. This place might be her destiny.
And it’s a destiny she shares with the woman in front of her.
Alonsa picks her up and carries her to the nearest building
Alonsa carries Chef to the local cobbler. He looks up from his diligent work on his footwear. "Oh, dear, what happened to her?"
“She passed out, I think it’s the heat.” He doesn’t need to know details. “Do you have any seats I can put her on”
"Don't see why not. Got some seats in the backroom, here." He opens a wooden door, motioning for Alonsa to enter.
Alonsa heads in.
There are indeed some seats, although none that look too awfully comfortable. There's a bench that Chef could be laid down on.
Alonsa lies her down on the bench, and sits on one of the chairs
She checks her again, to make sure she’s okay.
She's fine, as far as Alonsa can tell. The cobbler follows her in, and begins inspecting Penny's shoes. "Hm... definitely a couple sizes too large... might get to make a sale when she wakes, haha..."
Alonsa gets up from her chair, and hands the cobbler a small amount of money. “Keep an eye on her. I’m going to the sheriffs, tell her to meet me there when she wakes.”
He pockets the money, and nods. "No problem."
Perhaps it’s overly trusting to be doing this, but Alonsa is willing to bet that there’s something more going on with this girl. If it really is fate, then nothings going to happen to her.
Alonsa heads to the sheriffs office

The deputy sits in the front of the office, his legs kicked up on the desk. Seems like he was drifting off to sleep, but he quickly shakes it off as she enters. "Whu- Oh, uh... Howdy. Got an issue to report, or...?"
“The jails are here, yeah?”
"Yeah, visiting hours are still open. You here to see Thromb Cruor? If it's for the 'Bucky' girl, she's already been released, I think."
“Yeah, Thromb. I was also hoping to talk to the other one but I’ll see her later I guess.”
"Alright. Right this way. Got him in the holding cell." He stands up, and leads Alonsa further into the building.
Alonsa follows

They reach a room featuring bars, separating its sections from one another. Thromb sits behind them, still in his oversized winter coat. He doesn't seem surprised by Alonsa or the deputy's entrance, nor does he greet them as they enter.
“Hey…”
“How’s it going?”

"Been holed up in a cell all day. Sleeping on hard wood. It's not natural, and it's bad for my back." He stands up and approaches the bars. "That's not important. We need to get moving. The games are beginning."
((End session))
“The games? Oh, right, the games!”
“Sorry, been a long few days.”
"Yes. Too long." He pauses for a moment, before raising his hand and motioning for the deputy to step closer. "Guard! There's an issue!"
Alonsa is startled by the sudden movement
“I have been meaning to talk to you anyway… there’s been a lot of weird stuff happening.”

Thromb quickly glances back to Alonsa. "We can talk once I'm done with the guard."

The deputy raises his eyebrow, and steps towards Thromb. "What seems to be the proble-" Before he can finish his question, Thromb's arm lunges forward to the bars of the cell. As it should collide with the metal, the skin splits open, separating into separate slices of flesh that pass through the gaps in his containment. They conjoin back into the shape of a hand once past their prison's walls, and grip tightly around the deputy's neck.
“Holy shit!”
“Thromb, what the fuck?”
“How did you… how are you…”

"Hold on, almost done here." He reels his arm back, slamming the deputy's skull into the iron bars. His grip tightens, and the deputy begins to sputter out grunts of pain, struggling to free himself from Thromb's grasp. As he reaches for Thromb's hand with his own, his entire body suddenly goes limp, coinciding with an audible *snap*. Thromb releases his grip, and the deputy's body tumbles to the ground.
Alonsa is in complete shock.
“Thromb… Did you… You killed him?”
"Yeah, don't worry, he's not getting back up. What did you want to talk about?" He crouches down, and reaches into the deputy's pockets.
“Thromb, seriously!”
“What the fuck is happening?”
“Am I still dreaming?”
She backs away from him.
"I'm escaping from prison. You'll need me there to win the games." He retrieves a key from the deputy's pocket, and uses it to undo the lock keeping him trapped.
“You’re not explaining anything!”
“How are you… what are you? What the fuck?!!”
"Calm down. You're wasting your energy." He opens the door to his cell. "I'm a human, just like you. Biologically, at least. Philosophers might have a problem with that, but I don't care."
“Okay…. But….”
“How are you doing that?”
“And… how could you just kill that guy?!”
“Did you… did you actually kill the guy out there?!?”
“Shit…”

"Yondova's Emperor? No, that wasn't me. Why would I put it on display like that? I'm just here to protect my client, and sometimes I need to kill people that are in my way. That's how nature is. It's brutal, but it's fair. I was stronger, so the guard died." He steps over the deputy's corpse, and approaches Alonsa.
Alonsa trembles in fear.
“Why are you… protecting me? And don’t give me some bullshit like it’s because I’m paying you.”
“What im paying you isn’t worth… it’s not worth that man’s life!!”
“Oh god, I didn’t even know his name…”

"In nature, creatures protect their own. It ensures survival of their species... but if my survival is a guarantee, then what reason do I have to protect anyone? Well... it's the same reason you protect me, isn't it? You love me, Alonsa, and one day, I'll love you, too." He steps past Alonsa, and opens the door to the lobby.
“…What?”
“Thromb what the fuck does that mean?”
She follows him, more confused and angry than scared.
"Which part?" He leads her through the lobby, to the exit of the sheriff's office.
“All of it!!!!”
“The last part especially, though!”

"...Am I wrong? That is why you came to this town, right? Your capacity for love is overwhelming, almost without compare. You love each and every piece of history, capturing it within your studies, and there's nowhere richer in history than this town. I don't agree with it, but I can't deny how your love makes me feel." He steps out of the office onto the streets, heading for the saloon.
She runs in front of him, and walks backwards

“So, what, you’re like, the living embodiment of history, or something? I won’t deny that I love that stuff but… I can’t even begin to imagine how that would extend onto you. Sorry! I don’t mean to be mean, but you did just murder someone!!”
"It's your job as an archeologist to uncover the past, right? So go ahead, look at me. Tell me who I am. Also, keep it down about the murder, we don't want to run into trouble."
Alonsa looks him up and down
“I don’t know.”
“I don’t… I don’t understand any of this.”
“That doesn’t matter! The past is… the past is the past!” Alonsa always hated that phrase. “But we’re in the present, and you’re… like… I don’t know…”
“Is this related to whatever the shit is happening with the church?”

"Once you figure that out, that's when I'll love you. Your past is my present. Your present is my future. Let me love your world. Let me remember the shifting sands and the migrating fauna. That natural, everchanging beauty of the world you live in. All you need to do is love my world. This frozen painting. This town, too paralyzed to even eat its own tail. After all, that's all you have time for, isn't it?" 

He approaches the saloon, forcing Alonsa backwards through the door. Her back forces the entrance open, and is left exposed to its occupants. The wood creaks behind her, the sound growing closer by the second.
((End session))
Alonsa just slowly steps back, away from Thromb, not paying attention to what she’s walking into
"Careful. The trapdoor's open." Thromb points behind Alonsa. As she backs up, and approaches the noise, it becomes clear that it's not only coming from behind her, but below as well.
Alonsa turns around

A square of the wooden flooring has been moved to the side, revealing a ladder descending downward. As Alonsa notices this, a head emerges from the pit. She once again comes face to face with Briar McGregor.
Cory sighs upon stepping outside. "Sorry, just thought it'd be quieter in there."
"Its okay"

He lets go of Briar's hand, and starts a slow stroll down the street. "I've... got somethin' to get off my chest. Felt like y'all deserved to know. Narita... the bartender, not the, you know... I think she's tryin' to get under my skin 'bout it, but..."
She walks by his side, just listening to him talk.

"This town's... tough on a certain type of folk growin' up. I'm not exactly... from 'round here, uh, ancestor-wise. I was, well, second class, really. Had to work hard, doin' what I was 'spose to to scrape by... Then, uh, this girl, she... Well, she took interest in me. We rushed into things, I was young and foolish, 'course, but... really, I just think I wanted what she had. Rights, money, people who looked at her and saw... a person." His expression grows in discomfort at each sentence he forces out.

Briar looks over at his face, she wants to say something but she can't find the words. She extends her hand thinking of holding his hand to show support but she hesitates thinking if it's appropriate or not.

"So... we got hitched. Had a youngin. I didn't know how to handle it, it all happened so fast, and I was... too green. I wasn't ready to be... I try to do my best for them still, but we ain't together no more, so it's..." He fidgets with his hands, and his voice gets caught in his throat. "Look, I just thought you should know, there's a lotta baggage with... gettin' to know me."

She is very surprised and stays silent for a bit thinking. She steps in front of him and holds his hands "Thank you for telling me Cory... I- I don't really know what to say, I'm scared of saying something wrong all the time but I want you to know that it's okay. I still want to get to know you! I appreciate you trusting me enough to tell me, I won't lie and say it isn't a lot of information at once, how old is- Oh I don't know if I can ask that, I don't want to intrude when you already have a hard time talking about it... I'm sorry, I'm just rambling now"
He seems stunned for a moment, but his expression quickly softens. He gives her words a nod of acknowledgement. "Right. Thank y'all. Means an awful lot."
"Don't thank me, it's just how I feel" she smiles
"'Course." He stands there awkwardly for a moment, before clearing his throat. "That violin of yours ever turn up? Yondovan folk should have the luggage, still..."
"Oh! I should go ask soon, it will be so fun to play it for you and the others! I would also like the rest of my clothes"

He rubs the back of his neck, thinking something over. "Why don't I head on down to pick 'em up. You've still got the game at the saloon, 'n all... police ain't really welcome in that kinda crowd, so..."
Chills run down her spine "Oh I forgot about that... I'm very scared about it... Sorry- yeah, you can go get them for me, thank you so much Cory"

"I get it... Narita's got that air about her, but... she ain't gonna hurt you, missy. That ain't how she plays these, and even if it was..." He moves his hands out of her grasp, and places a palm on her shoulder. "She knows I'm in town, and I'll rain down bell if she tries any funny business."
"I will try my best to win" she smiles
"Oh! and Cory, thank you for trusting me"
He returns the smile. "You make it pretty darn easy." He lets go of her shoulder, and sets off on his own, offering Briar a wave as he leaves.
((End session))
She waves at him as he leaves. With a deep breathe she starts walking towards the saloon.

Briar arrives at the saloon. It's strangely desolate for the time of the day. Currently, only a single soul stands waiting behind the counter... but it's not Narita. Ace, dressed in bartending attire, wipes down a mug intently.
She walks up to him confused "Did you get a job here...?"

He jumps backward from her words, apparently having not noticed her entering. He nearly drops the mug, but catches it in mid-air. "Um... Well, uh... I... kind of ran up my tab last night... so... she said I could pay it off by doing some, y'know, part-time work...?"
"How much did you drink...?"
"..." He slings the towel he was cleaning with over his shoulder, and sets the mug down. "...A normal amount."
"Sure... Hm- Where is everyone else?" she looks around
"Oh, right, yeah." He walks around the counter, and bends down to examine a section of the floorboards. "They're... downstairs. That's where the games are played, apparently."
"Ohh, can you take me there?"
"...Are you sure about this? They seem kind of... intense, about this." He reaches his hands between the floorboards as he speaks. There's a small gap visible in a handful of them.
"I already agreed to be part so I don't have a choice anymore" she smiles nervously
He lifts up a piece of the floor, revealing a hatch leading down. There's a ladder descending into darkness. "Ladies... first?"
She nods and goes down the ladder slowly and carefully

The ladder has a sturdy construction, and is well maintained. There's little risk of a collapse, protecting Briar from what would surely be a fatal fall. Ace begins descending shortly after Briar, staying close above her. "What do you, well, figure the game will be...?"
She goes down slowly, trembling slightly afraid of slipping "Hm- I have no clue... I'm very scared about it but Cory said it should be fine and if anything happens he will be there for me"
"Yeah... I think it's, well, really nice, you know? To... have someone like that. A hero who can protect you. Who can... actually make a difference..."
"I'm glad I met him... he is really cute" she giggles, getting lost in her thoughts for a second
"Cute...? Isn't cuteness, like... for girls, though? Guys are supposed to be, you know... badass?"

"Everyone can be cute! Like Cory is very cool, being a sheriff makes him really 'badass' like you said, but when he smiles he is very cute" her face blushes as she keeps talking excitedly "In books it's that way, knights are brave and intimidating, but when they are with their princess they are caring and adorable"

"I haven't really... read any books like that. I just stick to reading books the Panthium clergy approves of, really..." Beneath Briar, the bottom of the ladder comes into view, and the volume begins to rise. There seems to be quite the commotion in the saloon's basement floor.
She gets off the ladder and looks at him waiting for him to get down too "I brought some of my books in my luggage, I will give you one of them"
She turns and looks at commotion trying to figure out what's happening

There's a sizeable crowd gathered in quite the dingy, dank room. Torches line the stone walls, with an unlit firepit on the opposite side of the floor from the entrance. Briar recognizes several of the patrons from the saloon. They're dripping with sweat, their faces red, cheering and jeering as they encircle the women who were performing as dancers two nights ago. Their role appears to have changed. They tear at each other, and swing their fists with abandon. They topple over each other into a pile on the floor made of fury and pain. One wraps her legs around the other's neck, attempting to strangle her. The crowd goes wild.
Her jaw drops as she stares at the scene, fear takes over her thoughts. Will she have to do something similar? What will she do? are the questions in her head.

Ace reaches the bottom of the ladder, and takes in the view as the women continue to struggle. The stranglehold is broken, and an attack is dealt in return. A crunching noise resounds across the room, as she slams her elbow into the women's chest. Blood is quickly coughed up in turn. 

"Um. Wow. Is... is that the game, or...?" Ace tries to subtly grab ahold of the ladder again.
"If that's the game, I will die here..." she takes a step back getting closer to the ladder too

Clap. Clap.

The entire room goes silent. The movement stills, and the crowd turns to face a figure by the firepit. The crowd is stained with sweat and blood, their faces red and their hair mangled. But the figure stands tall, her clothes clean, her hair perfectly combed, and an unstained face staring straight towards the ladder.

Narita's hands are pressed together, in mock cheer. "Welcome, welcome indeed. The game, yes, the main course can begin now."
"Main course...? This wasn't part of the game...?"

"Just an appetizer. This town is ravenous, quite ravenous, don't you know?" She snaps her fingers. "Grab them. Light it up."

The members of the crowd closest to the ladder roughly grab hold of Briar and Ace, preventing their escape, while those furthest from the ladder scramble to set the firepit ablaze.
Briar doesn't try to free herself, she just trembles terrified of what will happen

Ace almost seems to go limp, but he stares forward in equal portions of terror as Briar. The two of them are passed from person to person, shoved towards the center of the circle as the dancers fade into the crowd.

Narita steps into the circle as well, bringing her serene face close to Briar and Ace. The fire beginning to roar behind her casts the two in her shadow. "Shall we go over the terms of your debts, and today's prizes?"
Briar doesn't respond, she stares at the floor with her hand on her chest over her heart

"Mike Acilis... you've racked up quite the debt! You will be playing our game in order to work off your tab, that you were unable to pay last night. Sad, oh how sad it was." Her head almost seems to snap towards Briar. "Briar McGregor, your debt sits at... zero! You are free to go at any time. All you fight for is information for your beloved sheriff... well, that's not motivating, not very motivating at all, is it?"

She places a finger on her chin, lost in thought. She seems to settle on an idea, but in all likelihood, she had already known the terms of the game from the start. "How about we throw in a bonus prize for you! Yes, a bonus prize. In exchange for your success..."

Narita takes hold of Ace's hand. His fingers are taken into hers, enveloping him in her warmth, and then... he's enveloped in another warmth. She shoves his palm into the open flame of the firepit. He screams, tearing it away as his skin begins to sear.

"We will fogive Mike Acilis' debt, and spare his life!"
((End session))
Briar trembles terrified "Spare... his life?"
"Until his debt is repaid, his life is ours to do with as we please. That's not a guarantee he'll die, but..." She motions to the restless crowd. "They've built up quite the appetite."
She nods slowly "Cory made me think this wouldn't be so dangerous..."
she starts whispering to herself "I guess he said **I** wouldn't get hurt..."

"The slothful king of the pigs? Amusing, how amusing your faith is! Laugh with us!" She raises her arms, signaling for the crowd to erupt in boisterous guffaws. "He is a prop, a figurehead. He knows not but to be owned. By the church, by my family, and by his wife. He is allowed to keep the peace aboveground, but this is not his territory. Nor are you his people to protect. Foreigners, how disgusting, how vile!"
She is annoyed at those words but she can't push herself to say anything back. Terrified of saying the wrong thing in such a scary environment where she feels so small.
"Just... just start the game"

She smirks, and motions for a man to her side to step forward. It's the pianist from the bar. His size and build are somewhat average, but his expression glares with nothing but contempt for Briar and Ace. Ace himself is crouched on the ground beside Briar, clutching his roasted palm, tears in his eyes.

"Two against one. Your team has the advantage. Enjoy it." Narita disappears into the crowd.
"hm... so what... what are we supposed to do?" she looks down at Ace and back at the pianist
Ace gives her a befuddled look. "We? *We*? We can't do anything! We just have to wait... wait for a hero..." He clutches his head, and cowers before his opponent.
"Hm..." she looks around "I don't think we are getting one of those Ace..." she looks at the pianist open and down "Can we like chat instead of anything violent...?"
